_note: SYNTHETIC DEMO DATA. Roles, duties, questions and anchors are fictional and have not been validated. Question set v2.
organization: Minds in Motion (MiM), a fictional organization created for this demo

roles.title: Program Coordinator
roles.summary: Keeps MiM's workplace wellness workshops running on schedule: plans sessions, tracks enrollment, and keeps employer partners informed.
duties: Schedule and coordinate workshops with employer partners
Send updates and reminders to partner contacts

competencies.name: Planning & Organizing
competencies.definition: Schedules tasks and resources to meet deadlines.
questions: Tell me about a time you planned an event or workshop with a fixed date and limited resources. How did you schedule the tasks, and what was the result?
Describe a time when two deadlines conflicted. How did you decide what to do first, and how did it turn out?

anchors.1: Describes general intentions ("I stay organized") with no specific example of scheduling or prioritizing.
anchors.3: Gives a specific example of planning tasks or setting priorities; steps are partly described and the outcome is unclear.
anchors.5: Gives a specific example showing how tasks, timelines, and resources were sequenced; explains how priorities were set and the deadline or outcome that resulted.

competencies.name: Stakeholder Communication
competencies.definition: Shares clear, timely information with partners.
questions: Tell me about a time you had to tell an outside partner about a change in plans. How did you communicate it, and how did they respond?
Describe a situation where a partner misunderstood information you gave them. What did you do to clear it up?

anchors.1: Speaks generally about communicating well; no example of what was shared, with whom, or when.
anchors.3: Describes a specific communication with a partner; the message and timing are clear, but the partner's response or follow-up is not.
anchors.5: Describes what was communicated, how and when it was tailored to the partner, how understanding was checked, and the result.

competencies.name: Attention to Detail
questions: Tell me about a time you found an error in a report or record before it was shared. How did you catch it, and what did you do next?
Describe how you kept enrollment or tracking data accurate over time. Give a specific example.

anchors.1: Says they are detail-oriented without an example of catching or preventing an error.
anchors.3: Describes a specific error caught or check performed; the method is partly explained.
anchors.5: Describes a specific error caught or prevented, the checking method used, the correction made, and a step taken to keep it from happening again.

roles.title: Workshop Facilitator
roles.summary: Leads interactive, education-focused workshops on workplace well-being for employer teams, in person and online.
duties: Deliver MiM's standard workshop curriculum to groups of 10 to 40 employees
Adapt activities for in-person and virtual sessions
Guide group discussion so every participant can take part
Collect session feedback and suggest curriculum updates

competencies.name: Group Facilitation
competencies.definition: Guides group discussion and activities so participants stay engaged and on track.
questions: Tell me about a time you led a group session where participation was uneven. What did you do to involve more people, and what happened?
Describe a time a group discussion went off topic or became tense. How did you bring it back on track?

anchors.1: Describes presenting to a group but not how participation or discussion was managed.
anchors.3: Describes one specific technique used to engage the group; the effect on participation is partly described.
anchors.5: Describes specific techniques used to involve quieter participants or redirect discussion, how the group responded, and how the session goals were met.

competencies.name: Adaptability
competencies.definition: Adjusts approach when plans, audiences, or settings change.
questions: Tell me about a time you had to change your plan for a training or presentation at the last minute. What did you change, and how did it go?
Describe a time you delivered the same content to two very different audiences. How did you adjust your approach for each?

anchors.1: Describes a change in circumstances but not what they personally did differently.
anchors.3: Describes a specific adjustment to the plan or approach; the reasoning or result is partly explained.
anchors.5: Explains what changed, why the adjustment was chosen, how it was carried out, and the result for the audience or task.

competencies.name: Learning from Feedback
competencies.definition: Seeks and uses feedback to improve sessions.
questions: Tell me about a time you received critical feedback on a presentation or session. What did you change as a result?
Describe how you have collected feedback from participants and used it to improve something you delivered. Give a specific example.

anchors.1: Mentions receiving feedback but describes no change made in response.
anchors.3: Describes specific feedback and a change made; the impact of the change is unclear.
anchors.5: Describes how feedback was gathered or received, the specific change made, and evidence that the change improved the result.

roles.title: Partnerships & Outreach Specialist
roles.summary: Builds relationships with local employers and community organizations so MiM's programs reach their teams.
duties: Identify and contact prospective employer partners
Present MiM's programs to HR and leadership contacts
Keep partner records current in the contact database

competencies.name: Relationship Building
competencies.definition: Develops and maintains productive working relationships with external partners.
questions: Tell me about a time you built a working relationship with someone outside your organization from scratch. What steps did you take?
Describe a time a relationship with a partner or client became strained. What did you do to repair it?

anchors.1: Speaks generally about being good with people; no specific relationship or steps described.
anchors.3: Describes a specific relationship and some steps taken to build or repair it; the outcome is partly clear.
anchors.5: Describes specific, deliberate steps taken over time to build or repair a relationship, and a concrete result such as a renewed agreement or ongoing collaboration.

competencies.name: Persuasive Communication
competencies.definition: Presents information in a way that helps others make informed decisions.
questions: Tell me about a time you had to convince a decision-maker to try a new program, service, or idea. How did you make your case, and what was the outcome?
Describe a time someone raised an objection to something you proposed. How did you respond?

anchors.1: Describes the idea but not how the case was made or how concerns were handled.
anchors.3: Describes how the case was presented to a specific audience; handling of concerns is partly described.
anchors.5: Describes tailoring the case to the decision-maker's priorities, using evidence, responding to concerns, and the decision that resulted.

competencies.name: Follow-Through
competencies.definition: Tracks commitments and completes next steps on time.
questions: Tell me about a time you were managing follow-ups with several contacts at once. How did you keep track, and what was the result?
Describe a time you realized a commitment you made was at risk of slipping. What did you do?

anchors.1: Says they always follow up, with no example of a tracking method or a completed commitment.
anchors.3: Describes a specific method for tracking commitments; the outcome is partly described.
anchors.5: Describes a specific tracking method, how at-risk commitments were spotted and handled, and the commitments completed on time.
